# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
...

test.describe("opening balances", () => {
  test("opening balances", { tag: '@functionality' }, async ({ browser }) => {
    const sheet = ui.sheetId();
    const pg_uma = await ui.userPage(browser, "uma", sheet);
    await ui.setToday(pg_uma, "2026-03-25");
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "A", "pct": "10.00"})).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.setRate(pg_uma, {"grade": "B", "pct": "20.00"})).toBe(true);
    const p_ada = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ada", "grade": "A"}));
    const p_ben = ui.must(await ui.addPerson(pg_uma, {"name": "Ben", "grade": "B"}));
    expect(await ui.addPeriod(pg_uma, {"name": "P1", "from": "2026-03-01", "to": "2026-03-10"})).toBe(true);
    expect(await ui.addPeriod(pg_uma, {"name": "P2", "from": "2026-03-11", "to": "2026-03-20"})).toBe(true);

    expect(await ui.importOpenings(pg_uma, "Ada,P2,5.00\nbenny,P1,2.50")).toBe(2);

# Paste: a DRAFT claim per line of name,amount,date,note (the note may hold commas; a blank date is the sheet's
# today; the note may be absent), in order, for the person on the sheet with that name (ignoring case). Every line
# is checked first with the claim form's rules (and its name must be on the sheet); any line refused refuses the
# whole paste (400) and nothing is added. A note ending " #<reference>" gives the claim that external reference (not
# part of the note); one another claim on the sheet has, or an earlier line has, ignoring case, refuses the paste.
# A line whose person, date and note match one of their claims as they stood before the paste (void and deleted claims
# never match; lines never match each other) updates the newest such DRAFT to its amount instead of adding a claim
# (CLAIM_EDITED when the amount changes); a line whose matches include no DRAFT refuses the paste.
# Each line's claim is then opened by the user exactly as the open button would (CLAIM_OPENED, then its rollup lines),
# in paste order; any refusal the open button would give refuses the whole paste and writes nothing.
# Answers how many lines went through.

content.text:
Opening balances can now be pasted as `name,period,amount` lines, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**How it behaves**
- Every line is checked before anything is saved. The paste is refused, with the `opening-error` message shown and nothing written, if any line:
  - names a person who isn't on the sheet (by name or alias, ignoring case),
  - names a period that isn't on the sheet,
  - has an amount that isn't two decimals and 0.00 or more.
- Each line that goes through adds its amount to that person's carried figure for that period. It writes `OPENING_SET sheet=… by=… name=<the person's own name> period=… amount=…` to the audit file, so a line given as `benny` is recorded as `Ben`.
- The box shows how many lines went through (`opening-import-done`). The count clears when the button is pressed again.
- **Open periods:** the carried figure is the existing calculation plus the pasted openings.
- **Closed periods:** the carried figure is fixed at close and now includes the openings at that point. An opening pasted after the close is still saved and audited, but it doesn't change the shown figure until the period is reopened and closed again. This is what the test expects.

**Main changes**
- **Storage:** a new table, `src/main/resources/db/migration/V92__opening_balance.sql`.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `import-openings.POST.yml` under `rest/api/sheets/{sheetId}/`, with its classes in the new `opening` package. `PeriodCloser.java` now adds the openings into the carried figure when a period closes. The periods response has a new `personOpenings` field.
- **Screen:** a new paste box, `src/main/frontend/features/periods/ImportOpenings.tsx`, shown just after the periods list. `periods.ts` now adds the openings into the carried figure for open periods.

Cloning a sheet doesn't copy its opening balances. The request didn't mention cloning, so I left it out.
